goal: Extracts block-download state and logic out of PeerManagerImpl into its own class for easier testing and review
Aims to let block-download scheduling be unit- and fuzz-tested without the full net_processing stack
reviewability: Stale: needs rebase and conflicts with roughly a dozen other open PRs touching the same file
Reviewing now risks being invalidated by whichever competing PR merges first
agreement: Unaddressed objection: unclear if this decomposition direction is preferable to a competing PR, no resolution reached (Crypt-iQ)
Nonblocking objection: fuzz target's practical value is unproven and cs_main coupling may not really be reduced (maflcko)
Author produced a demonstration branch reconciling both approaches but no agreement was reached

categories.name: p2p
why: P3 because this is a large move-only reorganization with no correctness, performance, or lock-granularity benefit
cs_main remains the synchronizing lock throughout, so the benefit is limited to code organization and future testability
A maintainer questions whether this decomposition direction is even desirable versus a competing approach, and another maintainer doubts the fuzz target's proven value
